applicable_when: The kernel uses tl.dot with ALLOW_TF32=False, forcing all matrix multiply-accumulate operations through the FP32 scalar FMA pipeline (36.4% utilization). Enabling TF32 routes tl.dot through Tensor Cores, which deliver ~8x the throughput of FP32 FFMA on this GPU. K=480 is small enough that TF32 mantissa truncation (23->10 bits) will not accumulate error beyond atol=1e-3 for typical float32 inputs. Additionally, enabling USE_FAST_ACCUM=True avoids intermediate precision promotions in the accumulator, further boosting Tensor Core throughput.

applicable_when: The kernel is L1/shared-memory-bound, NOT DRAM-bound. The top two NCU rules (65.76% and 64.81% estimated speedup) both point to shared memory bank conflicts — 8-way average conflicts on 67% of all shared load wavefronts. The root cause is the B matrix access pattern: stride_bk=1, stride_bn=480 means B is stored column-major (K-major), so loading a [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] tile reads non-contiguous columns, causing threads in the same warp to hit the same shared memory bank repeatedly. Additionally, 168 registers/thread is extremely high, limiting occupancy to 18.75% (3 blocks/SM) and leaving only 2.94 active warps/scheduler — far too few to hide the shared memory latency (58.96% of cycles have no eligible warp). The fix is to introduce @triton.autotune with configurations that: (1) reduce BLOCK_M from 128 to smaller values (64, 32) to cut register pressure and allow more blocks/SM, (2) vary BLOCK_K to amortize the B-matrix transposed load overhead, (3) vary num_warps (4, 8) and num_stages (3, 4) to enable software pipelining that hides shared memory latency on H200 Hopper.
